title: You can hide it from people…
paragraphs:
You can hide it from people…
but you cannot hide it from God.

No one sees it when you worship.
No one notices it when you smile.
No one hears it when you pray.

And something in your life…
has already started to weaken because of it.
This is not just Achan’s story.

A glance.
A desire.
A whisper: “Just this once.”

A robe from Babylon.
Silver.
Gold.

It rarely looks dangerous at first.
It looks desirable.
“When I saw in the plunder a beautiful robe from Babylonia, two hundred shekels of silver and a bar of gold… I coveted them and took them. They are hidden in the ground inside my tent.”

I saw.
I coveted.
I took.
I hid.
That’s the anatomy of secret sin.
And maybe… that’s your pattern too.

You saw something you shouldn’t have.
You entertained something you knew wasn’t right.
You took a step you promised you wouldn’t.
But here’s the truth we avoid:

Into your peace.
Into your confidence.
Into your spiritual authority.
Israel lost a battle they should have easily won.
“I will not be with you anymore unless you destroy whatever among you is devoted to destruction.”

Not because He stopped loving them—
but because holiness matters.
And this is where it hits home.

“Why do I feel distant from God?”
“Why is my fire gone?”
“Why do I feel stuck?”
But maybe the real question is:
We’ve learned how to manage appearances.

We lift our hands…
while hiding our habits.

We quote Scripture…
while feeding secret struggles.

We look alive on the outside…
but something is buried underneath.
You think you’re getting away with it.
But you’re actually losing more than you realize.
Because God will not bless what you secretly protect.
This is where the story turns.
This is where grace breaks in.
But your story doesn’t have to end there.
Because someone else stepped into your place.

Where Achan was uncovered—
Jesus was stripped.

Where Achan bore judgment—
Jesus took wrath.

Where Achan paid for his sin—
Jesus paid for yours.
“God made him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.”

Every hidden thing.
Every buried compromise.
Every secret you hope no one finds—
But grace is not permission to keep burying sin.
Grace is the power to bring it into the light.
“If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins and purify us from all unrighteousness.”

Expose it before God—
so He doesn’t have to expose it through consequences.
God is not asking you to clean yourself up first.
He’s asking you to come out of hiding.
So let me ask you, heart to heart:

That habit?
That relationship?
That compromise?
That secret nobody knows?
Because the same God who exposed Achan…
offers mercy to you through Jesus.
And watch what God does with a heart that stops hiding.
